definition: An acid that is completely ionized in aqueous solution, such as $\ce{HCl}$, $\ce{HNO3}$ or $\ce{H2SO4}$; strong describes the extent of ionization, not the concentration.
An acid that is only partially ionized in aqueous solution, so its ionization equilibrium lies to the left, as for ethanoic acid.
A base that is completely ionized in aqueous solution, such as the group 1 hydroxides.
A base that is only partially ionized in aqueous solution, such as ammonia or an amine.
A reaction in which an acid reacts with a base to form a salt, often with water.
A technique in which one solution is added from a burette to a measured volume of another until the reaction is just complete, used to find an unknown concentration.
The point in a titration at which the amounts of acid and base added are in the exact ratio of the balanced equation.
The point in a titration at which the indicator changes colour; a good indicator makes it fall close to the equivalence point, but the two are different ideas.
